issues.description: Constructor mismatch for class StockIngredient: The problem statement UML and examples (problem_statement.md) specify and use a constructor StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity). The solution implementation (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/StockIngredient.java) provides a 3-parameter constructor StockIngredient(String, int, int). However, the template (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/StockIngredient.java) only defines a 4-parameter constructor StockIngredient(String, int, int, boolean). This prevents students from compiling or using the API as shown in the UML and the commented examples in Main, creating a blocking inconsistency.
issues.suggestedFix: Provide a 3-parameter constructor StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity) in the template repository. Preferably add it as an overload that delegates to the existing 4-parameter constructor (or add a 3-parameter constructor that implements the same validation/initialization logic as the solution). This will match the UML/problem statement and allow the example usages in Main to compile and students to instantiate StockIngredient as intended.

issues.description: Constructor signature mismatch for StockIngredient: The exercise description and examples (UML and Main) refer to a StockIngredient constructor with signature StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity). The solution implementation provides exactly that three-argument constructor (StockIngredient(String, int, int)). However, the template only defines a four-argument constructor StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity, boolean strictValidation) and does not provide a three-argument overload. A student following the problem text or the provided example usages (which use three arguments) will be unable to instantiate StockIngredient from the template and will get compilation errors, blocking progress.
issues.suggestedFix: Add a three-argument constructor to the template matching the problem statement and solution: implement an overloaded constructor StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity) that mirrors the solution behavior (validating/normalizing inputs as appropriate). Alternatively, keep the four-argument constructor but add a convenience overload that calls it with a sensible default for strictValidation. Do not change the problem statement examples to reference the four-argument form unless you explicitly document the additional parameter and its purpose.
